sources.title: Modelica Language Specification: the LaTeX source of each chapter
Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) 3.0: the AsciiDoc source of the standard (model exchange, co-simulation, scheduled execution)
System Structure and Parameterization (SSP) 2.0: the AsciiDoc source of the standard
GNU Octave manual: the Texinfo source of each chapter
GNU Octave functions: the Texinfo help of each function file, which the manual calls with @DOCSTRING

Scilab and Xcos: the help of every function and block (linear systems, control, signal processing, ODE solvers, optimization, Xcos palettes, FMU import), and the conversion of each MATLAB function to Scilab (m2sci)
sources.attribution: Dassault Systèmes, ESI Group, Scilab Enterprises, INRIA and the Scilab contributors

sources.title: The Modelica Standard Library 4.1: the documentation of each package, model, block and connector (Fluid, Thermal, Electrical, Mechanics, Blocks, StateGraph, Media, Magnetic, Math, Units...), taken from its Documentation annotations, and the Modelica language reference by keyword
OpenModelica User's Guide: OMEdit, OMShell, scripting (OMC API), simulation flags and solvers, FMI import and export, debugging, optimization, Python and Julia interfaces
FMPy: simulating, validating and inspecting FMUs from Python (command line, GUI, web app, Python API)
python-control: the Control Systems Library for Python (transfer functions, state space, time and frequency responses, lsim, step, bode, root locus, LQR, Kalman, MATLAB compatibility module)
sources.attribution: California Institute of Technology, Delft University of Technology and the python-control developers

sources.title: SciPy user guide: integration and ODE solvers (solve_ivp, odeint), signal processing (filters, LTI systems), optimization, interpolation, linear algebra, FFT, statistics, spatial algorithms
sources.attribution: Enthought, Inc. and the SciPy Developers

sources.title: SimPy: discrete-event simulation in Python (processes, events, resources, the environment, real-time simulation), its guides, examples and API reference
sources.attribution: Ontje Lünsdorf, Stefan Scherfke and the SimPy contributors
